takeaways: Every Caledonia call is still a check, not a finding. Nobody on the desk has read the Q3 release, and the headline's "back to normal" is meaningless without ounces, the prior-year quarter, and all-in sustaining cost (AISC). Because Proactive's headline already exists, the release may already be public, so pulling the primary document is the first task.

The Bilboes US$150M facility is the one item with a possible cash consequence. Undrawn availability is not a drawdown, so the desk should score only a disclosed draw in the MD&A liquidity section, the debt note, or the financing cash flows, and silence in those places is weak evidence of financing stress.

Timing is the main risk to our scoring. Q4 output, revised annual guidance, and Ivanhoe's Mari terms may first appear after 31 December, so an unresolved call should be recorded as "no result" rather than a miss, and deadlines should name the document that would carry the figure.

Cambria's 10.32 g/t over 7.5 m and 6.66 g/t over 15.0 m are intercept lengths, not true widths. They are encouraging, but they cannot enter a resource model until the company states an estimated true width with its orientation basis.

The Endeavour US$1.2bn Ivory Coast project and Ivanhoe's Pakistan deal are capital and deal-flow items with no supply effect before the late 2020s. The Codelco and Adani Kaburkaala MoU and the 42,100-tonne overstatement are reporting-reliability and credibility items, not tonnage events. South Africa's -7.5% September figure is a flash print that should not be stacked against Harmony's Q1 comparator until Stats SA data are in hand.

A strong profit line could then mask a weaker cost position, so the cost line deserves the closer read. (speculation level: medium)

Several mid-tier and major companies are now relying on partners to fund growth: Codelco with Adani, Ivanhoe with Mari, and Endeavour's funding mix is still undisclosed. If that pattern holds, the useful test for each deal is who carries the capex risk, not the headline size. (speculation level: high)

Enforcement announcements in Ecuador, Egypt, Ghana and Burkina Faso show activity, not output. The clean test would be whether official seizures or arrests are later reconciled against production or export data, which would show whether the crackdown changed supply at all. (speculation level: high)

chief_sessions.strategist_answer:
**Q1: What counts as a drawdown, and what would silence mean?**

A drawdown is a disclosed draw on the US$150M Bilboes facility: a stated amount taken, a debt balance that rises against that facility, or a financing inflow in the cash flow statement tied to it. Availability or commitment is not a drawdown. Holding an undrawn facility is a liquidity buffer, not a sign of stress.

Silence is weaker evidence than it sounds. If the Q3 release is out by 30 November, the MD&A liquidity section and the debt note should say whether the facility has been used, because a listed miner is normally expected to disclose material borrowing. So I would test the full filing, not the headline, and check three places: the liquidity discussion, the financing line in the cash flow statement, and the debt note. If none of them mentions the facility at all, that is informative, though it could also mean the facility is simply not material yet. I would not read it as a financing crisis.

The prediction should be scored on what the filing says as of its publication date. A drawdown after that date would not count, and I should say so in the note. Read together with the guidance cut, a drawdown would matter more than the facility's existence, because it would suggest cash generation is not covering the gap. I still hold this at low confidence, and I would move it only on the filing's wording.

**Q2: Which funding mix matters for Endeavour's US$1.2bn Ivory Coast project?**

The project is neutral if most of the capex is funded by non-recourse project debt, a partner's equity, or pre-payments tied to offtake or streaming. It starts to matter for balance-sheet risk if it is funded mainly from corporate debt or cash on hand while sustaining capex, dividends or buybacks continue, or if equity issuance is needed.

The threshold that matters is the ratio of the project's capex to the group's free cash flow and liquidity headroom, and I do not have Endeavour's financials in this material, so I cannot put a number on it. Historically, a mid-tier miner that funds a multi-year build from its own balance sheet is most exposed to a cost overrun or a gold price drop during construction. That is background, not a finding about Endeavour.

Until the funding structure is disclosed, I keep the project as a neutral capital commitment with no supply effect before 2028.

takeaways: Every Caledonia call is still a check, not a finding. Nobody on the desk has read the Q3 release, and the headline's "back to normal" is meaningless without ounces, the prior-year quarter, and all-in sustaining cost (AISC). Because Proactive's headline already exists, the release may already be public, so pulling the primary document is the first task.

The Bilboes US$150M facility is the one item with a possible cash consequence. Undrawn availability is not a drawdown, so the desk should score only a disclosed draw in the MD&A liquidity section, the debt note, or the financing cash flows, and silence in those places is weak evidence of financing stress.

Timing is the main risk to our scoring. Q4 output, revised annual guidance, and Ivanhoe's Mari terms may first appear after 31 December, so an unresolved call should be recorded as "no result" rather than a miss, and deadlines should name the document that would carry the figure.

Cambria's 10.32 g/t over 7.5 m and 6.66 g/t over 15.0 m are intercept lengths, not true widths. They are encouraging, but they cannot enter a resource model until the company states an estimated true width with its orientation basis.

The Endeavour US$1.2bn Ivory Coast project and Ivanhoe's Pakistan deal are capital and deal-flow items with no supply effect before the late 2020s. The Codelco and Adani Kaburkaala MoU and the 42,100-tonne overstatement are reporting-reliability and credibility items, not tonnage events. South Africa's -7.5% September figure is a flash print that should not be stacked against Harmony's Q1 comparator until Stats SA data are in hand.
creative: If Caledonia's Q3 ounces are near plan but full-year guidance is cut, the likely cause is a Q4 bottleneck in the blanket recovery, and the signpost is AISC rising while the gold price is high. A strong profit line could then mask a weaker cost position, so the cost line deserves the closer read. (speculation level: medium)

Several mid-tier and major companies are now relying on partners to fund growth: Codelco with Adani, Ivanhoe with Mari, and Endeavour's funding mix is still undisclosed. If that pattern holds, the useful test for each deal is who carries the capex risk, not the headline size. (speculation level: high)

Enforcement announcements in Ecuador, Egypt, Ghana and Burkina Faso show activity, not output. The clean test would be whether official seizures or arrests are later reconciled against production or export data, which would show whether the crackdown changed supply at all. (speculation level: high)
